chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Dāwūd the mawla of Abū al-Miʿzā, from one who informed him, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a woman who menstruates, then the time of her purity passes while she still sees blood. He said: “She should exercise precaution by waiting one day, if her menstruation is less than ten days. If the blood continues, then she is a mustaḥāḍah; and if the blood stops, she performs ghusl and prays.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: As for the woman in nifās, she is the one who delivers her pregnancy and blood comes out with it. She must refrain from salat (prayer), avoid sawm (fasting), and not approach the mosque, as we mentioned in the chapter of menstruation and the junub. When her blood stops, she checks herself just as the menstruating woman checks herself with cotton. If it comes out clean of blood, she washes her private part of it, performs wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer), then performs ghusl as we described for menstruation and janābah. But if blood appears on the cotton, she delays the ghusl until the end of the days of nifās, which is the cessation of the blood from her.

There has already passed earlier what indicates that she may not approach the mosque, and there is no disagreement among the Muslims that salat (prayer) and sawm (fasting) are not obligatory upon her during the days of her nifās. They differed only regarding the number of the days of her nifās, and after this, if Allah the Exalted wills, I shall mention what indicates that, and some of the reports that contain this subject.

key_terms.الصَّوْمَ: sawm (fasting), which is avoided during nifās
key_terms.الطُّهْرِ: ritual purity or the period of cleanliness from bleeding
key_terms.النُّفَسَاءُ: a woman in the state of nifās after childbirth
key_terms.الْحَيْضِ: menstruation, the legally recognized menstrual bleeding period
key_terms.الْغُسْلَ: ghusl, the full ritual bath required after certain states
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدَ: the mosque, which she may not approach in this state
key_terms.مُسْتَحَاضَةٌ: a woman experiencing istiḥāḍah, non-menstrual irregular bleeding

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings for prolonged bleeding after menstruation and for nifās in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This report addresses legal rulings concerning prolonged bleeding after menstruation and the rulings of nifās following childbirth. It distinguishes between ḥayḍ, istiḥāḍah, and nifās, and explains when a woman refrains from salat (prayer) and sawm (fasting), when she may not approach the mosque, and when wudu (ablution) and ghusl become necessary.
